From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@auroracorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: MSA + Exhibit consolidation for Q1 capacity uptick

Taylor —

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, Aurora is confirmed for the Q1 capacity increase (additional 220 GPU-hours/month) and we'd like to consolidate the standalone Exhibit C language into the main MSA to simplify signoff across procurement and engineering.

Attached is a working draft: "Aurora_Exhibit_C_consolidated_v1.docx" that folds the capacity schedule and billing cadence into an Exhibit A -> Exhibit C merge. High level asks:
- Can Aurora legal review the merged exhibit and provide redlines focusing only on (1) billing/proration, (2) SLA scope for burst capacity, and (3) data residency carveouts?
- Procurement: can we aim for a DocuSign path by end-of-day Monday 11/13? That keeps the Q1 provisioning schedule intact.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Aurora returns legal redlines by Fri 11/10 EOD
2) Redwood responds with consolidated redline by Mon 11/13 AM
3) Sign-off and DocuSign by Mon 11/13 EOD

If the schedule is tight, we can isolate the most time-sensitive clause (billing proration) into a short-term amendment and push the rest into a subsequent addendum.

Thanks — cc'ing Ben to confirm pricing and signpath.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@auroracorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@auroracorp.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA + Exhibit consolidation for Q1 capacity uptick

Sean —

Thanks for the draft. Procurement and legal reviewed the consolidation and attached a set of redlines ("Aurora_redline_from_legal_v2.pdf"). High-level feedback:
1) Billing/proration: we need explicit language for mid-term capacity additions (example: prorate at daily rate with a 7-day minimum notice).
2) SLA for burst capacity: Aurora requires a 99.5% availability SLA for dedicated pools or explicit fallback to dedicated preemption windows.
3) Data residency: we asked to retain the current clause that any customer data for AuroraCorp EU tenants must remain in eu-1 region; the consolidated draft appears to generalize residency.

Procurement asked for clarity on invoice cadence if we stack multiple upticks within a single quarter — can Redwood provide a sample invoice schedule?

We can meet your MAP but will need Redwood's legal to respond to the redlines; target Friday is still OK on our side if you can return consolidated redline Monday morning.

Regards,
Taylor Nguyen
Senior Counsel — Commercial
AuroraCorp

Attachment: Aurora_redline_from_legal_v2.pdf (pdf, 14 pages)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@auroracorp.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 07:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA + Exhibit consolidation for Q1 capacity uptick — Redwood consolidated redline

Taylor / Sean —

Thanks for the redlines, Taylor — good signal on the key items. I've attached Redwood's consolidated redline ("RI_consolidated_redline_v3.pdf") and summarize proposed compromises below so procurement has an immediate read:

1) Billing/proration — compromise language: prorate on a daily basis using the calendar month daily rate; if multiple mid-month upticks occur within a 30-day window, Redwood will combine into a single prorated invoice with line-item detail. (Accepts Aurora's 7-day notice ask, but we keep a 72-hour suspension right for suspected abuse.)

2) Burst SLA — we will add a dedicated pool option in Exhibit with 99.5% availability guaranteed for dedicated capacity. For hosted burst we propose an SLA target of 98.0% with an explicit fallback rule: if hosted burst misses target for two consecutive months, Redwood will offer temporary dedicated capacity for the following month at standard surge pricing.

3) Data residency — we reinstated explicit per-tenant residency language and flagged the eu-1 clause. We note that deployment-specific exceptions (customer-managed VPC) remain handled elsewhere.

Open items for procurement: invoice cadence example (attached as Annex A). Also: need Aurora to confirm whether the 7-day notice will be delivered by a named procurement contact (procurement@auroracorp.com is fine) or via the account portal.

If we get confirmation from Aurora this morning we can produce a clean DocuSign-ready file by EOD for your review.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | (650) 555-0123

Attachment: RI_consolidated_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 9 pages)
Attachment: Annex_A_sample_invoice_schedule.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

Taylor / team —

Quick note to confirm pricing: the 220 GPU-hours/month uplift maps to the pricing sheet in Annex A (line 4). No change to unit price — uplift will be invoiced at the committed monthly rate, with prorated charges per Laura's draft. We can also support a short-term pilot if Aurora wants to start the additional capacity before MSA fully executes; we'll need an SOW/pilot addendum for that.

If procurement can confirm the named contact for notices, we'll lock the MAP and get the DocuSign path ready.

Thanks —
